'''Yag'Dhul''' was a small [[Planet/Legends|world]] located in the [[Inner Rim/Legends|Inner Rim]] at the intersection of the [[Rimma Trade Route/Legends|Rimma Trade Route]] and the [[Corellian Trade Spine/Legends|Corellian Trade Spine]]. The complex interaction of orbits and rotations between Yag'Dhul and its three [[Moon/Legends|moons]] meant that the planet was continually beset by massive tidal forces powerful enough to pull the [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmosphere]] into different regions, exposing large areas of the surface to hard [[Vacuum/Legends|vacuum]].

It was the [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of the [[Givin/Legends|Givin]], who evolved a sealable [[exoskeleton]] that allowed them to survive in vacuum. The desire to maximize advantages had led the Givin to switch alliances as variables changed, such as when they had allied themselves with the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Separatists]] during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] era and later with the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]].

==Description==
===Planetology===
Orbiting a yellow [[Star/Legends|star]],<ref name="TKT" /><ref name="CEIII" /> Yag'Dhul was a small but dense [[Planet/Legends|planet]].<ref name="GG4" /><ref name="UAA" /> A gray [[Cloud/Legends|cloud]] cover made the world appear dull and colorless.<ref name="TKT" /> The planet possessed three large [[Moon/Legends|moons]] that orbited one another around a common center of gravity. At the same time, the moons and Yag'Dhul itself orbited a second shared center of gravity, as their combined mass amounted to roughly 70 percent of the planet's mass. This complex gravitational arrangement caused each moon and the planet to influence the motion of the others, creating a system that appeared highly erratic.<ref name="GG">''[[Galaxy Guide 4: Alien Races]]''</ref>

The presence of these three moons, together with a low-frequency retrograde rotation, resulted in some of the most severe tidal effects known in the [[The galaxy/Legends|galaxy]]. Yag'Dhul had a retrograde rotation with a period of 175 standard [[Standard hour/Legends|hours]], meaning it spun opposite to the direction of the moons' [[Orbit/Legends|orbit]]. Yag'Dhul and its moons completed their mutual orbital cycle in only 53 standard hours, resulting in a difference of 122 hours between the planet's rotational period and orbital cycle.<ref name="GG" /><ref name="GG4" />

As a result, Yag'Dhul's [[Ocean/Legends|oceans]] and even its [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmosphere]] flowed from one side of the planet to the other in patterns predictable only through the application of advanced mathematics.<ref name="GG4" /><ref name="NEGAS" /> As the atmosphere shifted, it boiled and swirled violently, generating powerful storms that filled the gray skies with lightning and illuminated flashes of red stone visible even from orbit.<ref name="BW">[[X-Wing: The Bacta War]]</ref>

At certain times of the [[Standard year/Legends|year]], the same three moons that wreaked havoc on Yag'Dhul's surface created especially perilous tidal conditions that extended the time required for [[Starship/Legends|ships]] to revert from [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] and navigate to new coordinates before returning to lightspeed.<ref name="MF">[[Millennium Falcon (novel)|''Millennium Falcon'']]</ref>

===Inhabitants===
====Natural challenges====
{{Quote|Hard to believe life could have arisen in that maelstrom. No wonder the Givin have an exoskeleton and can exist in a vacuum.|[[Wedge Antilles/Legends|Wedge Antilles]]|<ref name="BW" />}}
[[File:YagDhul-FF16.jpg|left|thumb|The planet Yag'Dhul]]
Yag'Dhul was the [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of the [[Givin/Legends|Givin]] people.<ref name="GG4" /><ref name="UAA" /><ref name="NEGAS" /> [[Scientist/Legends|Scientists]] marveled that a [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Species/Legends|species]] had even been able to develop on such a planet,<ref name="NEGAS" /> but the [[Blood/Legends|warmblooded]] Givin<ref name="GG4" /> somehow managed to overcome all ecological challenges.<ref name="NEGAS" /> To understand the evolution of the Givin and their world, it was necessary to fully appreciate the effect of the planet's enormous, unpredictable tides. One moment a being might have been standing beside a serene [[Water/Legends|pond]], gazing contemplatively at floating [[Flower/Legends|flowers]] and frolicking water [[Mammal/Legends|mammals]], while an hour later the lake might have been rushing past under the tremendous pull of Yag'Dhul's three moons, carrying with it the flowers, the frolicking mammals and even the surrounding air. Within two hours, all that remained of the lake was a frozen plain exposed directly to the hard [[Vacuum/Legends|vacuum]] of space.<ref name="GG4" />

Life on Yag'Dhul adopted two basic survival strategies to deal with this unpredictable environment. The first method was to remain mobile, so that when the water and the air rushed to the other side of the planet, the organism was carried along. The advantages of this were obvious, because under these conditions the organism was never exposed to the harsh conditions of vacuum. As a result, the unpredictability of the tides made it difficult to establish regular cycles for [[Reproduction/Legends|breeding]], feeding, [[Photosynthesis/Legends|photosynthetic]] activity, and other functions. In addition, the tides could carry the organism to the frigid polar regions one day and to the sultry equatorial areas the next, and surviving the rapid changes between such extremes presented its own challenges.<ref name="GG4" /> Strategies of mobile survival, for example, were followed by some animal species that traveled along with the tides.<ref name="SWE" />

The other survival strategy was for the organism to gradually seal itself against the vacuum, as the evolutionary ancestors of the Givin had done.<ref name="GG4" /> Their bizarre [[exoskeleton]], composed of impermeable outer [[Bone/Legends|bone]] plates connected by flexible membranes, formed a type of organic [[Environment suit/Legends|vacuum suit]] that sealed off all orifices and openings. To make use of this evolutionary adaptation, the Givin had to enter a state of [[Dream/Legends|hibernation]], which required them to gorge on large quantities of nutritious food beforehand. While sealed inside their exoskeletons, the Givin did not respire, instead producing all necessary energy from stored fats.<ref name="GG4" /><ref name="NEGAS" /> In addition, the Givin had developed a physiological ability to sense [[Barometer|barometric pressure]], allowing them to accurately anticipate tidal changes that required them to enter hibernation.<ref name="NEGAS" /> This solution, however, was imperfect. As the Givin became more physiologically complex, their energy requirements increased, making it impossible to simply remain inside the exoskeleton until the atmosphere returned.<ref name="GG4" />

====Intellectual society====
[[File:Givin_2.jpg|thumb|right|150px|A Givin]]
As the Givin grew more intelligent,<ref name="DB">{{DB|species|givin|Givin}}</ref> they realized that it was possible to predict the tidal patterns. Using advanced mathematics and complex formulas describing the orbits of the moons and the planet, they learned to determine the exact time, direction, and duration of tidal flows. Not surprisingly, the study of mathematics became a religion for the Givin, and mathematical law became the code by which they lived, with some priests even experimenting with «transcendental mathematics» and the development of formulas that could foretell the future.<ref name="GG4" />

All Givin [[Givin (language)|language]], culture, and religion centered on mathematics, which they credited with their ultimate salvation. The advanced study of equations was regarded as a highly devout pursuit – an attempt to reveal answers to the fundamental questions of life. With this central purpose, the Givin written languages were composed of thousands of specially defined mathematical symbols. Arithmetic even extended into Givin decorative arts and appeared in wall treatments and body adornments.<ref name="NEGAS" />

Mathematicians were the most powerful and revered members of Givin society, making it possibly the only example of a mathematocracy in the galaxy.<ref name="GG4" /> As befitted a mathematical [[theocracy]],<ref name="NEGAS" /> the most intelligent of the young Givin competed in mathematical contests for the right to enter monasteries dedicated to the study of mathematics. There, through ardent investigation and the assiduous application of quadratic equations, quantum theory, and the computational complexities of non-linear systems, they hoped to be graced with solutions to life's most complex equations, such as the meaning of life expressed mathematically – or, at the very least, to become leaders of their communities.<ref name="GG4" />

The Givin planetary [[Governor/Legends|governor]] was selected through contests involving the calculation of multidimensional differentials. All political decisions were also made according to the guidelines of null-modal probability by ruling bodies known as the [[Body Calculus]] and the coalition of Factors, although the respective responsibilities of these bodies were not disclosed to outsiders. Givin religious practices were led by extraordinarily gifted mathematicians who served as priests and lorekeepers.<ref name="NEGAS" />

The Givin resided in [[City/Legends|city-shelters]] composed of hermetically sealed buildings capable of withstanding even the most severe ravages of the planet's tides.<ref name="GG4" /><ref name="UAA" /> All Givin cities were located on high [[Mountain/Legends|mountain]] peaks, where the danger posed by the rampaging oceans was minimal, and their [[Spaceport/Legends|spaceports]] were constructed underground.<ref name="LoE" />

==History==
===Republican era===
====Early history====
[[File:Caulbon-EGTW.jpg|left|thumb|Yag'Dhul was located on the edge of explored space]]
On the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] Yag'Dhul, the [[Givin/Legends|Givin]] were [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]] [[Species/Legends|aliens]] with extremely durable [[exoskeleton]]s and ghastly visages. They had evolved their exoskeletal structure in response to their homeworld's frequent environmental shifts, which regularly left vast portions of the planet without [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmosphere]].<ref name="UAA" /> Givin [[Priest/Legends|priests]], deeply engaged in the study of the mathematical mysteries of their planet's rotation, could predict these patterns with such accuracy that their species were able to keep their homes stable and peaceful and,<ref name="NEGAS" /> during low tide, routinely [[Mining/Legends|mined]] the deepest ocean floors.<ref name="GOI" /> This also enabled Givin to mine the world's natural resources, making them a generally wealthy species with a stable economy.<ref name="NEGAS" />

Guided by the absolute insights of mathematics, Givin society had developed extremely advanced technology.<ref name="GG4" /> Givin monasteries devoted themselves to unraveling the meaning of life through complex equations, and every young Givin dreamed of being the one who solved the final formula. This devotion to numbers made the Givin particularly useful beyond their homeworld. Givin [[Starship/Legends|ships]] used computers only for data storage, as the Givin calculated [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] vectors in their heads more quickly than most [[Navigation computer/Legends|navigation computers]].<ref name="UAA" />

The Givin were far from the first civilization to master interstellar travel. Yag'Dhul became part of the [[Galactic community]] around [[20,000 BBY/Legends|20,000 BBY]] during the so-called [[Great Manifest Period/Legends|Great Manifest Period]] and alongside the settlement of the [[Trailing Sectors/Legends|Trailing Sectors]] by the nascent [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]].<ref name="TEA" /> During the early stages of the [[Alsakan Conflicts/Legends|Alsakan Conflicts]], Yag'Dhul joined the [[Corellia/Legends|Corellian]] [[Corellian Hegemony|faction]], which refused to take part in the disputes between [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] and [[Alsakan/Legends|Alsakan]].<ref name="EGW" />

====The development of the shipbuilding industry====
[[File:YagDhulsIntersection.jpg|thumb|right|220px|Yag'Dhul was located at the intersection of the Rimma Trade Route and the Corellian Trade Spine]]
The subsequent [[Millennium/Legends|millennia]] of space exploration pushed back the borders of known space and improved Yag'Dhul's strategic position.<ref name="TEA" /> By the 5500s BBY,<ref name="TEA" /> the [[Herglic Trade Empire|Herglic Trade Empire]] and the merchants of the [[Tapani sector/Legends|Tapani sector]] spurred the expansion<ref name="AoR">[[Star Wars: Age of Rebellion Core Rulebook|''Star Wars: Age of Rebellion'' Core Rulebook]]</ref> of an ancient [[Herglic/Legends|Herglic]] route known as the [[Hidakai Pool]],<ref name="CEII35">{{CSWECite|II|35|Herglic space}}</ref> which extended from the [[Colonies/Legends|Colonies]] into the southern regions, thus created the [[Rimma Trade Route/Legends|Rimma Trade Route]]. At the same time, this developing route, along with the less prosperous [[Corellian Trade Spine/Legends|Corellian Trade Spine]] and the [[Hydian Way/Legends|Hydian Way]] at the strategically important [[Eriadu/Legends|Eriadu]],<ref name="AoR" /> increased in length two thousand [[Standard year/Legends|years]] later and furthered the long boom, knitting the region together for [[Merchant/Legends|traders]] from across the galaxy.<ref name="TEA" /> Situated at the intersection of the Rimma Trade Route and the Corellian Trade Spine,<ref name="NEGAS" /><ref name="TEA" /><ref name="EoE">''[[Star Wars: Edge of the Empire Core Rulebook]]''</ref> Yag'Dhul became a major reversion point and the site of skirmishes dating back millennia.<ref name="MF" />

The Givin made excellent shipwrights,<ref name="UAA" /> and the [[Yag'Dhul shipyards|shipyards]] that circled Yag'Dhul produced sturdy and elegant starships that competed on a level matched only by those of the [[Duros/Legends|Duros]] or the [[Verpine/Legends|Verpine]].<ref name="GOI" /> The Givin were heavily involved in the transport of goods and could be found throughout the galaxy thanks to their sleek, fast starships. However, these ships were of little use to other species, as the Givin took full advantage of their peculiar physiology to save weight and increase cargo space, pressurizing only their sleeping quarters.<ref name="GG4" /> With their voluminous cargo vessels, the Givin ran one of the galaxy's largest and most efficient shipping and transport businesses.<ref name="NEGAS" /> Beyond the sphere of shipwrights, the Givin became an important galactic manufacturer, with high-technology computer goods among their common exports. They achieved such success largely through activities conducted off their homeworld, following the [[Colonist/Legends|colonization]] of more stable neighboring worlds.<ref name="LoE" />

====Separatists crisis====
{{Quote|It is not without regret that the Body Calculus and the collected domain and range of the Givin people have decided to leave the larger Republic. But the threats of remaining are greater than or equal to the threats of secession.|[[Daggibus Scoritoles]]|<ref name="HNN54" />}}
Yag'Dhul remained part of the Galactic Republic for millennia, except for a brief period during the [[Jedi Civil War]] when it was [[Battle of Yag'Dhul (Jedi Civil War)|conquered]] by [[Darth/Legends|Darth]] [[Revan/Legends|Revan's]] [[Darth Revan's Sith Empire|forces]]. Nevertheless, the long-standing alliance between Yag'Dhul and the Republic came to an end with the onset of the massive [[Separatist Crisis/Legends|Separatist Crisis]], which engulfed the galaxy nearly a millennium after the [[Ruusan Reformations/Legends|Ruusan Reformations]].<ref name="TEA" />

[[File:YagDhulInCIS.jpg|left|thumb|230px|Joining Yag'Dhul to the CIS provided the Separatists with access to, and control of, the Rimma Trade Route and the Corellian Trade Spine]]
In the final [[Standard month/Legends|months]] leading up to the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]],<ref name="NEC" /> as the splintering of the Republic became increasingly common, the [[Body Calculus]] on the planet Yag'Dhul, together with the collective domain and range of the Givin people, [[Secession of Yag'Dhul|decided]] to leave the larger Republic. Senator [[Daggibus Scoritoles]] transmitted Articles of Secession via the [[HoloNet/Legends|HoloNet]] to the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Senate]] in the morning, making the separation official. In the process, he expressed regret that the decision had been made but emphasized that «the threats of remaining were greater than or equal to the threats of secession». The statement was also simulcast across the broadcast towers of Yag'Dhul's largest civic shelters. The transmission was accompanied by numerous charts and graphs explaining the action. According to the broadcast, the Body Calculus's most revered mathematicians had developed functional models of the Republic's political situation. By advancing the model along its time axis, the resulting projections indicated a bleak future for both the Republic and Yag'Dhul specifically.<ref name="HNN54" />

====The war that divided the galaxy====
{{Quote|It's not just bigger cannons and faster ships that will win this war. The importance of leading-edge astrogational data and hyperspatial calculations cannot be overstated. With the correct transdimensional computations, a skilled astrogator could conceivably move a warship across the galaxy in a fraction of the standard duration.|[[Wat Tambor/Legends|Wat Tambor]], the [[Foreman/Legends|Foreman]] of the [[Techno Union/Legends|Techno Union]], placed great hopes on the Givin's contribution as allies of the Confederacy|<ref name="IC73">{{InsiderCite|73|CIS Shadowfeed Dispatch 15:01:15 Edition}}</ref>}}
Consequently, the planet seceded, and the native Givin later served as mathematicians for the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]], discovering new [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlanes]] for the war effort<ref name="IC73" /> and contributing [[Wavecrest-class frigate|''Wavecrest''-class frigates]]<ref name="CSD-15:3:21">{{InsiderCite|76|CIS Shadowfeed Dispatch 15:3:21 Edition}}</ref> from their well-regarded shipyards. The planet served as the base for the [[Confederate First Fleet|First Fleet]] of the [[Confederate Navy/Legends|Confederate Navy]]. Its shipbuilding capabilities were apparently destroyed during or after the Clone Wars, but the industrious Givin rebuilt them by the time of the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]].

===Under the Empire and the rise of the New Republic===
[[File:GivinNEGAS.jpg|thumb|left|120px|A [[Givin/Legends|Givin]]]]

The planet's politics were complex, but certain factions in the government supported [[Yag'Dhul insurgents|resistance]] against the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. An [[Empress-class space station|''Empress''-class space station]] named [[Yag-prime]] was built by the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] over Yag'Dhul during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]].

After the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], the planet was under the control of [[Warlord/Legends|Warlord]] [[Sander Delvardus]]. The [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] [[Battle of Yag'Dhul (Galactic Civil War)|freed]] the planet in [[5 ABY/Legends|5 ABY]].<ref name="TEA" />

However, Warlord [[Zsinj]] held the station Yag-prime in [[6 ABY/Legends|6 ABY]]. The station was [[Raid on Yag-prime|captured]] from his forces by the New Republic,<ref name="TKT" /> and became, with the permission of the Givin government, the site of [[Rogue Squadron/Legends|Rogue Squadron's]] orbiting base for training during the [[Bacta War]]. The New Republic maintained official possession of the station until the Givin demanded that it be ceded a few years after the [[Pellaeon–Gavrisom Treaty]].

The planet joined the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] sometime between [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]] and [[9 ABY/Legends|9 ABY]]. It was a New Republic stronghold during the [[Thrawn campaign]].<ref name="TEA" />

===Yuuzhan Vong War and the years that followed===
<div style="float: right">[[File:BattleOfYagDhul.jpg|thumb|200px|The Battle of Yag'Dhul]]</div>

The planet was contested during the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]] at the [[Battle of Yag'Dhul (26 ABY)|Battle of Yag'Dhul]], the [[Yuuzhan Vong]]'s intention being to take Yag'Dhul to use it as a staging ground for an assault on [[Thyferra/Legends|Thyferra]]. With Thyferra, Yag'Dhul was said to have been [[Battle of Yag'Dhul (29 ABY)|secured]] by [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances|Galactic Alliance]] forces before the retaking of [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]].

Despite their [[Speciesism|xenophobic]] tendencies, the Givin were members of the Galactic Alliance, seeing such membership as a statistical advantage to their people's economy and political well-being. At that time, any [[Ambassador/Legends|ambassadors]] who worked with the Givin had to undergo extensive education in mathematics in order to negotiate with them, lest they found themselves at a considerable disadvantage. At some point no earlier than [[36 ABY]], Yag'Dhul was described in a [[The New Essential Guide to Alien Species (book)|guide]] to various species of the galaxy that was based on the research notes of [[sentientologist]] [[Mammon Hoole]].<ref name="NEGAS" /> By [[137 ABY]], the homeworld of the Givin lay within the boundaries of [[Darth Krayt's Galactic Empire]].<ref name="TEA" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Planet08-SWR.png|right|thumb|The planet Yag'Dhul in the game ''Star Wars: Rebellion'']]
The PC game [[Star Wars: Rebellion (video game)|''Star Wars: Rebellion'']] mistakenly places Yag'Dhul in the [[Glythe sector/Legends|Glythe sector]] of the [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]]. In addition, in the game, Yag'Dhul was depicted as a lifeless planet, pockmarked with craters and with a barely visible atmosphere.
